name: Corporate Law
title: Corporate Lawyer
intro: Corporate law involves advising businesses on mergers, acquisitions, governance, compliance, and commercial transactions. It is one of the highest-paying legal specializations in India, with Tier-1 firms paying premium salaries to fresh graduates.
whoShouldPursue: Students drawn to business, finance, and transactional work
Those comfortable with high-intensity, deadline-driven environments
Individuals seeking structured law firm career progression
Candidates who enjoy negotiation and deal-making over courtroom litigation
eligibility: BA LLB or LLB from a recognized university
Bar Council enrollment (AIBE clearance)
Strong internships at law firms or corporate legal departments
NLU degree provides significant advantage for Tier-1 firm entry
workDesc: Drafting, negotiating, and closing commercial transactions while advising companies on regulatory compliance and corporate governance.
workExamples: Advising on a large-scale M&A deal between two listed Indian companies
Drafting and reviewing complex shareholder agreements and joint venture contracts
Handling SEBI compliance and regulatory filings for a publicly listed corporation
futureOutlook: India's growing deal ecosystem, SEBI regulatory expansion, and startup boom ensure sustained high demand for corporate lawyers through 2030.

name: Environmental Law
title: Environmental Lawyer
intro: Environmental law deals with legal frameworks governing pollution control, biodiversity conservation, climate change, and sustainable development. Practitioners appear before the National Green Tribunal and advise governments, NGOs, and corporations on environmental compliance.
whoShouldPursue: Individuals passionate about environmental protection and climate justice
Those interested in public interest litigation and policy advocacy
Students comfortable working across government, NGO, and corporate sectors
People who want to combine legal expertise with science and ecology
eligibility: LLB or BA LLB from a recognized university
Bar Council enrollment mandatory
LLM in Environmental Law is a strong advantage
Background in environmental science or policy is helpful but not required
workDesc: Representing clients in environmental disputes, advising on regulatory compliance, and advocating for sustainable development through legal frameworks.
workExamples: Filing a PIL before the National Green Tribunal to halt illegal mining in a biodiversity hotspot
Advising a manufacturing corporation on ESG compliance and environmental clearance requirements
Representing a community affected by industrial pollution in seeking remediation and compensation
futureOutlook: Rising climate regulations, ESG mandates, and Green Tribunal expansion are driving rapid growth in environmental law demand across India.

name: Human Rights Law
title: Human Rights Lawyer
sub: Human Rights & Social Justice Legal Practice
intro: Human rights law focuses on protecting fundamental rights, representing marginalized communities, filing Public Interest Litigations, and advocating for civil liberties. Practitioners work with NGOs, UN agencies, and legal aid organizations.
whoShouldPursue: Individuals driven by social justice and advocacy for vulnerable communities
Those passionate about constitutional rights and civil liberties
Students who prefer mission-driven work over purely commercial legal practice
People comfortable with public speaking, campaigning, and community engagement
eligibility: LLB or BA LLB from a recognized university
Bar Council enrollment mandatory
LLM in Human Rights Law is advantageous
Prior experience with NGOs or legal aid organizations is valued
workDesc: Representing victims of rights violations, filing PILs, and advocating for policy reforms to protect civil liberties and human dignity.
workExamples: Representing bonded laborers in a Supreme Court case seeking enforcement of anti-trafficking laws
Filing a PIL challenging discriminatory practices against marginalized communities
Advocating at an international human rights body on digital privacy rights for Indian citizens
futureOutlook: Growing digital rights concerns, ESG accountability standards, and global human rights frameworks are expanding opportunities for human rights lawyers.

name: International Law
title: International Law Specialist
intro: International law covers cross-border disputes, treaty obligations, international trade, arbitration, and diplomatic legal matters. Practitioners work at international courts, UN bodies, global law firms, and government foreign affairs divisions.
whoShouldPursue: Those fascinated by geopolitics, diplomacy, and global governance
Students with strong multilingual abilities and cross-cultural awareness
Individuals seeking careers with international mobility and global exposure
Candidates who enjoy complex, multi-jurisdictional problem-solving
eligibility: LLB or BA LLB from a recognized university
LLM in International Law strongly preferred
Bar Council enrollment required for domestic practice
Proficiency in at least one foreign language is highly advantageous
workDesc: Advising on cross-border disputes, treaty negotiations, international arbitration, and trade law matters across multiple jurisdictions.
workExamples: Representing India in a WTO dispute settlement panel on agricultural trade subsidies
Advising a multinational corporation on cross-border M&A compliance across three jurisdictions
Serving as legal counsel at an international court on a complex case
futureOutlook: India's expanding FDI inflows, growing outbound M&A activity, and increasing participation in international arbitration are creating strong demand for international law specialists.

name: Tax Law
title: Tax Lawyer
intro: Tax law involves advising individuals, corporations, and governments on income tax, GST, transfer pricing, customs duty, and international tax structuring. It is one of the most recession-proof legal specializations with consistently high demand.
whoShouldPursue: Those with a strong aptitude for numbers, accounting, and financial analysis
Students who enjoy statutory interpretation and regulatory complexity
Individuals seeking stable, high-demand legal careers with structured growth
Candidates comfortable with continuous learning as tax laws evolve frequently
eligibility: LLB or B.Com LLB from a recognized university
Bar Council enrollment mandatory
B.Com background provides significant advantage
ADIT or specialized tax certifications are valued additions
workDesc: Advising clients on tax planning, representing them in ITAT and High Court litigation, and structuring cross-border transactions for tax efficiency.
workExamples: Defending a multinational corporation in a large transfer pricing dispute before the ITAT
Advising a startup on GST registration, classification, and input tax credit optimization
Structuring a cross-border joint venture to optimize tax implications under India's DTAA network
futureOutlook: India's new Income Tax Code, GST maturity, and BEPS/Pillar Two implementation are creating unprecedented demand for specialized tax lawyers through 2030.

name: Legal Research
title: Legal Researcher
intro: Legal research encompasses academic scholarship, policy analysis, legislative drafting, and doctrinal study of law at universities, think tanks, and government bodies. Researchers shape legal reform through published scholarship and evidence-based policy recommendations.
whoShouldPursue: Those passionate about deep analytical study of legal theory and jurisprudence
Students who enjoy writing, publishing, and contributing to legal scholarship
Individuals seeking academic or policy-oriented careers over litigation
Candidates with strong research methodology and critical thinking skills
eligibility: LLB from a recognized university
LLM preferred for research positions
PhD required for senior academic and research roles
UGC-NET qualification essential for university teaching positions
workDesc: Conducting in-depth legal research, publishing scholarly papers, analyzing policy implications, and contributing to legislative reform through evidence-based recommendations.
workExamples: Publishing a peer-reviewed paper on constitutional interpretation of digital privacy rights
Conducting a commissioned study for the Law Commission on reforming India's criminal justice system
Developing policy briefs for a government think tank on data protection legislation
futureOutlook: Growing demand for evidence-based legal policy, the expanding NLU system, and increasing government focus on legal reform are sustaining steady demand for legal researchers.

name: Counselling Psychology
title: Counselling Psychologist
intro: Counselling psychology focuses on helping individuals navigate life transitions, emotional challenges, stress, and relationship issues through evidence-based therapeutic techniques. Unlike clinical psychology, it primarily addresses everyday emotional and adjustment concerns rather than severe mental disorders.
whoShouldPursue: Individuals with deep empathy and strong interpersonal listening skills
Those drawn to helping people manage stress, grief, career transitions, and relationships
Students interested in private practice or corporate employee wellness
People who prefer a therapeutic approach over diagnostic or clinical work
eligibility: BA Psychology or B.SC Psychology from a recognized university
MA/M.SC Psychology with counselling specialization
Postgraduate diploma in guidance and counselling is a valuable addition
Relevant supervised counselling hours for practice
workDesc: Providing therapeutic support to individuals, couples, and groups facing emotional, relational, and career-related challenges through structured counselling sessions.
workExamples: Conducting individual therapy sessions for professionals dealing with workplace burnout
Facilitating couples counselling for relationship conflicts and communication breakdowns
Running stress management workshops for corporate employees under an Employee Assistance Programme
futureOutlook: Rising mental health awareness, corporate wellness mandates, and expansion of teletherapy platforms are driving strong and sustained demand for counselling psychologists in India.
deg: MA/M.SC Psychology + M.Phil/PsyD for clinical practice

pathways.degree: MA/M.SC Psychology + M.Phil/PsyD for clinical practice

name: Organizational Psychology
title: Organizational Psychologist
intro: Organizational psychology applies psychological principles to workplace settings, focusing on employee selection, performance management, leadership development, and organizational change. It is a high-compensated non-clinical psychology specialization in India.
whoShouldPursue: Those interested in the intersection of psychology and business management
Students with strong analytical and data-driven thinking
Individuals who enjoy working in corporate HR, consulting, or talent strategy
Candidates seeking high compensation in the psychology field
eligibility: BA/B.SC Psychology from a recognized university
MA/M.SC Psychology with industrial-organizational specialization
MBA HR with a psychology background is a strong combination
Psychometric assessment certifications add significant value
workDesc: Designing employee assessment tools, advising on organizational development, leading leadership coaching programs, and analyzing workplace behavior to improve productivity and engagement.
workExamples: Developing psychometric assessment frameworks for hiring at a large company
Designing and implementing an employee engagement survey and action plan for a 5000-person organization
Leading an organizational change management program during a corporate merger
futureOutlook: Growing corporate investment in employee wellness and data-driven HR practices are creating premium demand for organizational psychologists.
deg: MA/M.SC Psychology + M.Phil/PsyD for clinical practice

pathways.degree: MA/M.SC Psychology + M.Phil/PsyD for clinical practice

name: Educational Psychology
title: Educational Psychologist
intro: Educational psychology applies psychological principles to learning and education, addressing learning disabilities, student mental health, curriculum design, and academic interventions. Practitioners work in schools, universities, EdTech companies, and special education centers.
whoShouldPursue: Those passionate about improving educational outcomes for students
Individuals interested in child development and learning processes
Students who enjoy working with children, adolescents, and educational institutions
People drawn to special education, inclusive learning, and academic research
eligibility: BA/B.SC Psychology from a recognized university
MA/M.SC Psychology with educational specialization
B.Ed combined with psychology background is valuable
RCI registration required when working with children with disabilities
workDesc: Assessing learning difficulties, designing educational interventions, counselling students on academic and emotional challenges, and advising schools on inclusive education practices.
workExamples: Conducting psychoeducational assessments to diagnose learning disabilities in school children
Designing an anti-bullying intervention program for a school network
Advising an EdTech company on personalized learning approaches based on cognitive psychology research
futureOutlook: NEP 2020 emphasis on student wellness, school counsellor mandates, and EdTech growth are creating structured and expanding demand for educational psychologists.

name: Social Research
title: Social Researcher
intro: Social research involves systematic investigation of social phenomena, communities, and human behavior using qualitative and quantitative methods. Researchers work at universities, think tanks, international development organizations, and government agencies to inform policy and program design.
whoShouldPursue: Those fascinated by understanding social structures, patterns, and human behavior
Students who enjoy fieldwork, surveys, data collection, and analysis
Individuals seeking careers in policy research, the development sector, or academia
Candidates comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies
eligibility: BA/MA Sociology from a recognized university
MA Anthropology provides an alternative pathway
BSW/MSW qualification is valuable for development research
PhD required for senior academic research positions
workDesc: Conducting social surveys, analyzing community data, evaluating program impact, and producing evidence-based reports for policy formulation and social intervention design.
workExamples: Designing and conducting a large-scale household survey on migration patterns in urban India
Evaluating the impact of a government mid-day meal scheme on primary school enrollment rates
Producing a policy brief on employment discrimination for a national think tank
futureOutlook: India's growing focus on evidence-based policy, social impact measurement, and data-driven governance is sustaining steady demand for trained social researchers.
